fact_text: As of 11 Nov 2025, about 265,000 companies were registered in Pakistan, but only 543 were listed on the stock exchange, roughly 0.2% of registered firms.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Are So Few New Companies Listing on the PSX?' (YouTube, 2025-11-11)

fact_text: Only 11 new companies listed on the PSX in 2024, and only one new company listed in 2023.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Are So Few New Companies Listing on the PSX?' (YouTube, 2025-11-11)

fact_text: The reporter noted that the market was hitting new highs in Nov 2025 while investors had cash but too few new companies to invest in.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Are So Few New Companies Listing on the PSX?' (YouTube, 2025-11-11)

fact_text: The video says a company seeking a KSE-100 index listing must have operated in its business for 3 years before listing and have made profits for 2 years.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Are So Few New Companies Listing on the PSX?' (YouTube, 2025-11-11)

fact_text: The video says a listed company must keep at least 20 crore rupees of capital after listing, otherwise the company can be delisted.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Are So Few New Companies Listing on the PSX?' (YouTube, 2025-11-11)

fact_text: Listed companies must publish financial statements annually, half-yearly or quarterly, have their accounts audited each year, and upload these documents to their website.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Are So Few New Companies Listing on the PSX?' (YouTube, 2025-11-11)

fact_text: The IPO listing process starts with appointing a consultant or book runner, then applying to the PSX and SECP, which review the application before the IPO date is announced.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Are So Few New Companies Listing on the PSX?' (YouTube, 2025-11-11)

fact_text: Officially the listing approval process takes 15 days to one month, according to the video.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Are So Few New Companies Listing on the PSX?' (YouTube, 2025-11-11)

fact_text: New companies offer investors little information beyond the balance sheet, so investors find it hard to judge management's commitment and whether the share price will hold after an IPO.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Are So Few New Companies Listing on the PSX?' (YouTube, 2025-11-11)

fact_text: Uber's 2019 IPO was priced at $45 per share, and the reporter said the stock fell about 40% within weeks of listing.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Are So Few New Companies Listing on the PSX?' (YouTube, 2025-11-11)

fact_text: The reporter attributed the fall in Uber's shares after its 2019 IPO to growth figures the company had misstated and weak financial condition.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Are So Few New Companies Listing on the PSX?' (YouTube, 2025-11-11)

fact_text: Investors prefer companies that have been in the market for a long time and whose business models they understand, because that lowers the risk of uncertain returns.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Are So Few New Companies Listing on the PSX?' (YouTube, 2025-11-11)

fact_text: The reporter said owners often avoid listing because it brings public questions on decisions, results and losses, and Pakistani owners generally dislike answering such questions.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Are So Few New Companies Listing on the PSX?' (YouTube, 2025-11-11)

fact_text: The reporter argued that owners may stay unlisted to avoid scrutiny, since a listed company's profits and tax position become harder to hide.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Are So Few New Companies Listing on the PSX?' (YouTube, 2025-11-11)

fact_text: The video says listing makes it easier to raise money and gives companies a fair market valuation.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Are So Few New Companies Listing on the PSX?' (YouTube, 2025-11-11)

fact_text: The reporter said that if tax compliance were common in Pakistan, about half of the economy's problems would already be solved.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Are So Few New Companies Listing on the PSX?' (YouTube, 2025-11-11)

fact_text: The reporter's view is that more listings need a simpler IPO process and a fixed tax regime, so that owners are not deterred by visibility.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Are So Few New Companies Listing on the PSX?' (YouTube, 2025-11-11)
